Sanshirō had also linked him to a horse incident at the main gate, which Hirota confirms. Sanshirō wonders whether the train companion is truly Hirota, which he decides is likely but admits is a stretch. He complains that his sister is foolish and refused to let Hirota go home, insisting he stay at the hospital. {"entries":[{"name":"赤シャツ","reading":"あかシャツ","category":"character","keys":["赤シャツ","教頭"],"content":"Akashatsu is a vice-principal (教頭) and a 文学士 (Bachelor of Arts) who speaks in an oddly gentle, feminine voice. He wears a flannel undershirt even in hot weather and wears red shirts all year round, claiming it is good for his health. The narrator finds his clothing ridiculous and feels that it mocks other people. He invites the narrator fishing, laughing with a loud ホホホホ, and he assumes he has won the argument over the morality of fishing. On the boat trip he admires the pine trees and the scenery, and he objects when the narrator asks to land on the island. When the narrator says he will confront Horita, Akashatsu becomes alarmed and warns him against violence, which the narrator sees as an attempt to protect himself. Afterwards he asks the narrator to keep what happened the previous day to himself and to say nothing to others, sweating as he makes the request. He agrees to drop the matter if the narrator finds it troublesome, and he asks the narrator again whether he is all right. The narrator finds him inscrutable and suspects that he is distrusting him, which the narrator resents, since he himself would never go back on a promise."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"Ｋ","reading":"ケー","category":"character","keys":["Ｋ"],"content":"The narrator's childhood friend from the same home region, whom the narrator names only as Ｋ. Ｋ was the second son of a Shinshu Buddhist priest, and while the two were in middle school he was adopted into a wealthy doctor's family, changing his surname. His adoptive family paid for his studies, and after he moved to Tokyo he boarded in the same lodging house as the narrator, sharing a room with him. In Tokyo the two feared the city and its people, yet boasted in their room of becoming great men, and Ｋ was the stronger of the two in this ambition. Raised in a temple, he constantly used the word 精進 (shōjin, single-minded devotion), and the narrator saw all his conduct as described by this one word. The narrator secretly held Ｋ in deep reverence."}]}

He still delivers newspapers to the Campanella house every morning."},{"name":"カムパネルラ","reading":"かむぱねるら","category":"character","keys":["カムパネルラ","カムパネルラさん"],"content":"Campanella is a schoolboy in Giovanni's class who readily raises his hand to answer the teacher's question about the Milky Way. When called on, he stands but cannot answer. He is Giovanni's close friend, and the two once looked at a large book about the Milky Way together in the study of Campanella's father, a doctor. Giovanni suspects Campanella did not answer right away out of kindness, to spare Giovanni's feelings. Campanella never teases Giovanni about his father's broken promise of a sea otter jacket, and looks sorry for him when others do. His house once had a toy train running on an alcohol lamp, and Giovanni often stopped there on his way home from school. Campanella's father and Giovanni's father were friends since childhood."},{"name":"銀河","reading":"ぎんが","category":"term","keys":["銀河","天の川","銀河帯"],"content":"The Milky Way, shown as a pale, cloudy band across a large black star chart hung in the classroom. People have called it a river or a stream of milk, but the teacher explains that through a large telescope it appears as many small stars. The teacher uses a model with glowing grains in a lens to explain that we live inside this stream of stars, and that distant parts look dense and faintly white. The teacher says that our sun is also a star that shines by its own light, and that today is a festival of the Milky Way, so the students should go outside and look at the sky."},{"name":"ジョバンニの母","reading":"じょばんにのはは","category":"character","keys":["お母さん","ジョバンニのお母さん"],"content":"Giovanni's mother is ill and rests in the front room of their small house, wrapped in a white cloth. She is glad when Giovanni brings home sugar cubes and asks whether the milk delivery came. She is gentle with Giovanni and tells him to eat first. She says his father once was a close friend of Campanella's father."},{"name":"ジョバンニの父","reading":"じょばんにのちち","category":"character","keys":["お父さん","ジョバンニのお父さん"],"content":"Giovanni's father is away, and Giovanni believes he has been at sea fishing. Giovanni's mother fears he may not have gone out to sea. Giovanni insists he could not have done anything bad enough to be put in prison. He once gave the school a large crab shell and deer antlers, which are kept in the specimen room, and he promised Giovanni a sea otter jacket."},{"name":"ジョバンニの姉","reading":"じょばんにのあね","category":"character","keys":["姉さん","ジョバンニの姉"],"content":"Giovanni's older sister went out and came back around three in the afternoon. Before leaving, she tidied the house and made a tomato dish for Giovanni and their mother."},{"name":"ジョバンニの家","reading":"じょばんにのいえ","category":"place","keys":["家","小さな家"],"content":"Giovanni's home is a small house in a back street, one of three attached houses in a row. The left entrance has an empty box planted with purple kale and asparagus, and its two small windows have awnings kept down. Inside, the mother rests in the room by the entrance."},{"name":"ラッコの上着","reading":"らっこのうわぎ","category":"item","keys":["ラッコの上着"],"content":"A sea otter jacket that Giovanni's father promised to bring him. Other children tease Giovanni about the promise, but it has not been fulfilled."},{"name":"アルコールラムプの汽車","reading":"あるこーるらむぷのきしゃ","category":"item","keys":["汽車","アルコールラムプで走る汽車"],"content":"A toy train at Campanella's house that runs on an alcohol lamp. Its rails form a circle, with electric poles and signal boards, and the signal light turns blue only when the train passes. When the alcohol ran out, they used kerosene and the boiler became covered in soot."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"カムパネルラのお父さん","reading":"かむぱねるらのおとうさん","category":"character","keys":["カムパネルラのお父さん","博士"],"content":"Campanella's father is a doctor with a pointed, pale chin who was once a friend of Giovanni's father. When Campanella goes missing in the river, he stands among the townspeople and students, dressed in black and holding a watch, staring at the water. He declares firmly that there is no hope, because Campanella has been in the water for forty-five minutes. Even so, he gazes at the Milky Way reflected in the river. He politely thanks Giovanni for coming, asks whether Giovanni's father has returned, and says he received a cheerful letter from him two days earlier and expected the ship to arrive about now. He invites Giovanni and the other boys to visit his house after school the next day."},{"name":"ジョバンニの父","reading":"じょばんにのちち","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニの父","お父さん","ジョバンニのお父さん"],"content":"Giovanni's father is away, and Giovanni believes he has been at sea fishing. Giovanni's mother fears he may not have gone out to sea. Giovanni insists he could not have done anything bad enough to be put in prison. He once gave the school a large crab shell and deer antlers, which are kept in the specimen room, and he promised Giovanni a sea otter jacket. Campanella's father says he received a cheerful letter from him two days before the festival and expected his ship to arrive about that night, but that the ship must have been delayed. Giovanni has not yet seen him return."},{"name":"ジョバンニ","reading":"じょばんに","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニ","ジョバンニさん"],"content":"Giovanni is a schoolboy in class at the afternoon lesson. When the teacher asks about the Milky Way, he raises his hand but cannot answer clearly, and he blushes as Zanelli laughs at him. He remembers reading about the stars with Campanella at Campanella's house, and he feels sad because he has been tired from hard work, less lively at school, and talking less with his friends. After school he hurries home to his mother, who is ill and resting, and brings her sugar cubes for her milk. He eats tomato and bread, and says he believes his father will return soon because a newspaper reported good fishing in the north. He still delivers newspapers to the Campanella house every morning. On the night of the Milky Way festival he carries warm milk bottles and goes out with Campanella and their friends, and later hears that a child has fallen into the river. He runs to the river and finds Maruso, who tells him that Campanella jumped in after Zanelli and has not been found. At the river, Campanella's father tells him Campanella is hopeless, and Giovanni wants to say he was walking with Campanella that night, but he is too choked up to speak. Campanella's father thanks him and invites him to visit the next day. Giovanni then runs back toward town to tell his mother that his father will return."},{"name":"カムパネルラ","reading":"かむぱねるら","category":"character","keys":["カムパネルラ","カムパネルラさん"],"content":"Campanella is a schoolboy in Giovanni's class who readily raises his hand to answer the teacher's question about the Milky Way. When called on, he stands but cannot answer. He is Giovanni's close friend, and the two once looked at a large book about the Milky Way together in the study of Campanella's father, a doctor. Giovanni suspects Campanella did not answer right away out of kindness, to spare Giovanni's feelings. Campanella never teases Giovanni about his father's broken promise of a sea otter jacket, and looks sorry for him when others do. His house once had a toy train running on an alcohol lamp, and Giovanni often stopped there on his way home from school. On the festival night he goes to float lanterns on the river with Giovanni, and when Zanelli falls into the water, Campanella jumps in and pushes Zanelli toward the boat. Afterward he cannot be found, and the people searching the river include his father. His father declares him beyond help after he has been in the water for forty-five minutes. Some of the townspeople still imagine he might appear from among the waves or be standing on some unknown sandbar, waiting for someone to come."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"宗彭沢庵","reading":"しゅうほうたくあん","category":"character","keys":["沢庵","沢庵さん","宗彭沢庵"],"content":"Takuan (沢庵) is a young Zen monk from Tajima province, about thirty years old, who stays at the temple for a time. He is a cheerful, playful man who often makes Otsū laugh, such as when he wanders out naked to dry his robe and mimics the Buddha at the Buddha's birthday rite. He claims to be a reincarnation of Siddhartha, and he speaks of human suffering and desire, and he hopes Otsū can be spared from it."},{"name":"お通","reading":"おつう","category":"character","keys":["お通","お通さん"],"content":"Otsū (お通) is a young orphan raised at the Shippōji temple, and she is sixteen years old. She is the fiancée of Matahachi and is also connected to Takezō, who is her betrothed as well as Matahachi's friend; both men were pressed by her and their families to stay home. She is cold and lonely in manner, like the ash of an incense burner, and is waiting in the village while the men are away at war. Her lonely moods are often lifted by the young monk Takuan, who stays at the temple and makes her laugh. In the spring, she gathers wild flowers with a sickle and basket by the Aida River, and she worries that Matahachi and Takezō are dead because no word has come from either of them."},{"name":"宮本武蔵","reading":"みやもとむさし","category":"character","keys":["宮本武蔵","武蔵","武やん","武蔵さん"],"content":"Takezō (武蔵), seventeen years old, lies among the dead on the battlefield at Sekigahara after the army he served has been defeated. He is wounded, with bullets likely lodged in his body, and is too weak to move. He left his village with his friend Matahachi against the wishes of his mother, his fiancée Otsū, and Matahachi's family, hoping to win glory as a soldier. Since joining the Shinmen household's forces, he has mostly been assigned menial tasks such as cutting grass rather than fighting. No word has come from him or Matahachi since the war, and by the fourth month of spring Otsū fears they are both dead."},{"name":"新免伊賀守","reading":"しんめんいがのかみ","category":"character","keys":["新免伊賀守","伊賀守"],"content":"Shinmen Iga-no-kami (新免伊賀守) is the lord of the domain where Takezō and Matahachi's village lies, and he heads the Shinmen household. Members of his family did not return from the war. Villagers say that the small castle is now occupied by warriors of the Tokugawa side whom no one in the village knows."},{"name":"英田川","reading":"あいだがわ","category":"place","keys":["英田川","あいだがわ"],"content":"The Aida River (英田川) flows past the village, about four or five chō downstream from it. Its riverbank is covered with spring wild flowers, where Otsū goes to gather flowers and grass."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"吾輩","reading":"わがはい","category":"character","keys":["吾輩"],"content":"The narrator, a cat who says he has no name yet. He was born in a dark, damp place and was first taken in hand by a student (書生). After being abandoned in a bamboo grove, he found his way into a house and was repeatedly thrown out by the maid おさん. He later mentions visiting the neighbouring cat 三毛 through a hole in the bamboo fence."},{"name":"書生","reading":"しょせい","category":"character","keys":["書生"],"content":"A student who lived in the house and was the first human the narrator saw. The narrator describes him as the most fierce of humans, and says he was said to catch cats, boil them and eat them. He picked up the narrator, carried him around, and then left him in a bamboo grove."},{"name":"おさん","reading":"おさん","category":"character","keys":["おさん"],"content":"A maid in the house the narrator sneaks into. She is rougher than the student, grabs the narrator by the scruff of the neck and throws him out onto the street. The narrator repeatedly crept back into the kitchen and was repeatedly thrown out, and he resents her for it, including for an earlier theft of a mackerel (三馬) he committed against her."},{"name":"三毛","reading":"みけ","category":"character","keys":["三毛","隣家の三毛"],"content":"A cat who lives in the house next door. The narrator visits her through the gap in the bamboo fence, and he still uses that route to see her up to the time of writing."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"吾輩","reading":"わがはい","category":"character","keys":["吾輩"],"content":"The narrator, a cat who says he has no name yet. He was born in a dark, damp place and was first taken in hand by a student (書生). After being abandoned in a bamboo grove, he found his way into a house and was repeatedly thrown out by the maid おさん. He later mentions visiting the neighbouring cat 三毛 through a hole in the bamboo fence. Finally thrown into the kitchen by the maid, he decides to make this house his home. Few in the household value him, so he attaches himself to the master, sitting on his newspaper-reading knees and lying on his back when he naps. He prefers sleeping with the two small children, though when he does they wake and cry, and the master rushes in and once beat his rump with a ruler."},{"name":"主人","reading":"しゅじん","category":"character","keys":["主人","この家の主人"],"content":"The master of the house, a teacher who is rarely seen by the narrator because he shuts himself in his study after school. The family thinks he is a hard worker, but the narrator sees him napping and drooling on his books; he has a weak stomach, takes Takadiastase after big meals, and is nervous and neurasthenic. He says little, twists the black hair under his nose while thinking, and complains to his friends that teaching is very hard. He lets the narrator stay, and the narrator often sits on his lap or back."},{"name":"細君","reading":"さいくん","category":"character","keys":["細君"],"content":"The master's wife in the house where the narrator lives. She became very angry when the narrator scratched and polished his claws on the tatami, and afterwards he was not easily let into the main room."},{"name":"小供","reading":"こども","category":"character","keys":["小供","子供"],"content":"The master's two small children, aged five and three, who sleep together in one bed in a separate room. The narrator tries to sleep between them, but when one wakes and cries that a cat has come, the whole household comes running. The narrator considers them selfish: they turn him upside down, put a bag over his head, throw him out, or push him into the stove, yet they become furious if he tries to fight back."},{"name":"白君","reading":"しろくん","category":"character","keys":["白君"],"content":"A cat living in the house opposite (筋向い) whom the narrator respects. He tells the narrator at every meeting that humans are the most unfeeling of creatures. He recently gave birth to four kittens, but the student of his house took them to the back pond on the third day and drowned them."}],"other_names":[]}

{"entries":[{"name":"苦沙弥","reading":"くしゃみ","category":"character","keys":["主人","この家の主人","苦沙弥先生","苦沙弥君","苦沙弥"],"content":"The master of the house, a teacher known as 苦沙弥先生, whom the narrator rarely sees because he shuts himself in his study after school. The family thinks he is a hard worker, but the narrator sees him napping and drooling on his books; he has a weak stomach, takes Takadiastase after big meals, and is nervous and neurasthenic. He says little, twists the black hair under his nose while thinking, and complains to his friends that teaching is very hard. He lets the narrator stay, and the narrator often sits on his lap or back. His old friend 鈴木君 visits him after a long separation of about ten years."},{"name":"白君","reading":"しろくん","category":"character","keys":["白君"],"content":"A cat living in the house opposite (筋向い) whom the narrator respects. He lives in the house of a military man. He tells the narrator at every meeting that humans are the most unfeeling of creatures. He recently gave birth to four kittens, but the student of his house took them to the back pond on the third day and drowned them. He weeps while telling this story and argues that cats must fight and destroy humans to live in a proper family life."},{"name":"三毛","reading":"みけ","category":"character","keys":["三毛","三毛君","隣家の三毛"],"content":"A cat who lives in the house next door, whose master is a lawyer (代言). The narrator visits her through the gap in the bamboo fence, and he still uses that route to see her up to the time of writing. She is indignant that humans do not understand ownership, since they seize the food cats find."},{"name":"鈴木","reading":"すずき","category":"character","keys":["鈴木君","鈴木"],"content":"An old friend of 苦沙弥先生 who visits his house, having found it by following the ペンペン草 (shepherd's purse) that the master had mentioned. Ten years have passed since they last met, and the master looks him up and down in surprise. He has neatly parted hair, wears an English-tailored tweed suit, a flashy collar, and a gold watch chain, so he does not seem to the narrator like the master's old friend at all."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"田中誠","reading":"たなかまこと","category":"character","keys":["田中誠","誠","田中兄"],"content":"Tanaka Makoto is a third-year high school student and captain of the baseball team. He is the older brother of Tanaka Sho. Their teacher calls him \"田中兄\" to tell him apart from his younger brother. He picks Sho up from class after school and asks him to come watch his next game. He is pitching on the mound in that game."},{"name":"田中翔","reading":"たなかしょう","category":"character","keys":["田中翔","翔","田中弟"],"content":"Tanaka Sho is a first-year student and the younger brother of Tanaka Makoto. In class he is called \"田中弟\" to distinguish him from his brother. He sits next to Yamamoto Hanako, and he asks her about the book she is reading. He invites Hanako to watch his brother's game."},{"name":"山本花子","reading":"やまもとはなこ","category":"character","keys":["山本花子","花子","花子ちゃん","花子さん","山本さん"],"content":"Yamamoto Hanako is a girl who sits next to Tanaka Sho in class and is usually quietly reading a book. Sho calls her 花子ちゃん, and she shows him the cover of her book when he asks about it. Makoto greets her as 山本さん and thanks her for looking after his brother. She later comes with Sho to watch Makoto's game, sitting beside him in the stands and waving to Makoto on the mound."}]}
